A hydrogen cylinder doesn't move easily, and it doesn't ask permission about where it sits in your lab. H-Genie Lite does both. It's compact enough to fit in any fume hood, and light enough in footprint to relocate wherever hydrogen is actually needed, generating hydrogen from water up to 50 bar, on demand. Set a pressure or a time, press start. That's the whole workflow, stated to be learnable in one minute. Internal hydrogen leak detectors run continuously, and it's built from the same R&D 100 award-winning H-Genie platform, just streamlined down to the essentials.

faqs.question: What is the H-Genie® Lite used for?
faqs.answer: It's a standalone hydrogen gas generator, used to replace a hydrogen cylinder by producing hydrogen from water on demand, up to 50 bar.

faqs.question: What quality water does the H-Genie Lite need?
faqs.answer: Deionized water with a recommended conductivity below 1 µS/cm.

faqs.question: Where should the H-Genie Lite be used?
faqs.answer: In a ventilated laboratory fume hood, which it's specifically sized to fit, and it can be relocated to wherever hydrogen is needed next.

faqs.question: How do I set up the H-Genie Lite for a run?
faqs.answer: Set the required pressure or time on the touchscreen, then press start; the workflow is stated to be learnable in about one minute.

faqs.question: How do I extend runtime for longer or unattended operation?
faqs.answer: Add the Automatic Water Filler accessory, which detects a low tank and refills automatically from a built-in or external water source, monitoring Millipore Milli-Q water quality throughout.

faqs.question: Can the H-Genie Lite perform reactions like deuteration?
faqs.answer: No. It generates hydrogen gas; it doesn't run chemical reactions itself. Reactions like deuteration are performed by systems such as the H-Cube, which this generator could potentially supply.

faqs.question: Can generated hydrogen be stored?
faqs.answer: The system is built for on-demand generation and use; storage isn't described in the confirmed materials, and this is worth confirming directly with Inkarp for your specific setup.

faqs.question: Is the H-Genie Lite compatible with ThalesNano's fleet systems?
faqs.answer: Yes, via the Automatic Water Filler accessory, which connects to the Phoenix – H-Genie platform or the broader Instrument Fleet through the same THS System Controller used with H-Cube Advance.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the H-Genie Lite and the full H-Genie?
faqs.answer: The Lite is a streamlined, more affordable version focused on essential features; full comparison detail against the H-Genie II is confirmed by Inkarp.

body: This generates hydrogen. It doesn't run reactions. Unlike a flow reactor with hydrogen generation built in, H-Genie Lite is a standalone source, meant to replace a cylinder wherever hydrogen gas is actually needed.
The safety story is continuous monitoring, not just avoided cylinders. Internal hydrogen leak detectors run alongside the on-demand generation itself.
Simplicity is a stated, specific claim. Set a pressure or a time, press start, learnable in one minute.
It's built to move. Compact enough for any fume hood, and relocatable to wherever the next job needs hydrogen.
It comes from a real award-winning platform. The full H-Genie is an R&D 100 award winner; this is the streamlined, more affordable version of that same core system.
Water quality matters here too. Deionized water below 1 µS/cm conductivity, with a 3-liter reservoir supporting 200 mL/hr of consumption.
It connects into ThalesNano's broader automation ecosystem. The Automatic Water Filler accessory bridges this system to the same THS fleet control used with H-Cube Advance.

sections.title: Safety systems and water requirements
body: Replacing a hydrogen cylinder only works if the replacement is genuinely safer, and that comes down to continuous monitoring, not just a different generation method.

Internal hydrogen leak detectors run throughout operation, alongside whatever other safety features the system carries. Water quality has its own requirement too: deionized water below 1 µS/cm conductivity, consumed at 200 mL/hr from a 3-liter reservoir, which gives a working runtime before a refill is needed. The recommended installation, a ventilated fume hood, is stated directly rather than left implicit.
